hook: A nursing mother entered a 268-mile race through the British winter. She beat everyone.
story: The Spine Race runs the length of England's Pennine Way in January: 268 miles of snow, bog and darkness, and the clock never stops. In 2019, Jasmin Paris entered - a veterinary lecturer from Edinburgh with a baby daughter at home. She took the lead early and held it. At the checkpoints, while her rivals slept, she expressed milk for her baby. After 83 hours, she crossed the finish line alone.
number: The course record stood at 95 hours and 17 minutes, set by a man. Paris finished in 83:12. She didn't edge the record; she removed twelve hours from it.

full_text: A nursing mother entered a 268-mile race through the British winter. She beat everyone. The Spine Race runs the length of England's Pennine Way in January: 268 miles of snow, bog and darkness, and the clock never stops. In 2019, Jasmin Paris entered - a veterinary lecturer from Edinburgh with a baby daughter at home. She took the lead early and held it. At the checkpoints, while her rivals slept, she expressed milk for her baby. After 83 hours, she crossed the finish line alone. The course record stood at 95 hours and 17 minutes, set by a man. Paris finished in 83:12. She didn't edge the record; she removed twelve hours from it. Five years later, she became the first woman ever to finish the Barkley Marathons. By 99 seconds.
